title: Add VPC module with subnet + routing defaults
author: Victor Alvarez
commits: vpc: initial module scaffold + variable interface
vpc: create public/private subnets per AZ with opinionated CIDR splitting
vpc: route tables + IGW routes for public subnets
vpc: NAT gateway strategy (per-AZ default, single-NAT optional)
vpc: add EKS subnet tags + default resource tags
docs: add design notes + constraints section
ci: wire terraform fmt/validate on examples + modules
body: Summary: This PR implements the core `modules/vpc` module for the Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha). The goal is to provide a Redwood-validated default VPC layout suitable for Redwood Private deployments that run on EKS (assumed) with private worker nodes and conservative routing defaults. This module focuses on: VPC creation, public/private subnet layout across AZs, route tables, and a NAT strategy with explicit trade-offs documented. Motivation: Technical discovery/pilots keep getting blocked on basic networking variability (subnet layouts, route tables, NAT/egress assumptions). We want a default that works for most enterprise VPC baselines while remaining composable with future modules (endpoints/logging/iam) and customer-specific connectivity (VPN/DX) without forcing premature complexity. What’s included: (1) VPC with DNS enabled by default: `enable_dns_support=true` and `enable_dns_hostnames=true`. (2) Subnet layout: public + private subnets per AZ (min 2 AZs recommended). CIDR splitting is opinionated but overridable via explicit subnet CIDRs. (3) Routing: public subnets route `0.0.0.0/0` to an Internet Gateway; private subnets route `0.0.0.0/0` to NAT Gateway(s). (4) NAT strategy defaults: default is NAT Gateway per AZ (`one_nat_gateway_per_az=true`) to avoid cross-AZ dependency and improve fault isolation; optional `single_nat_gateway=true` for cost-sensitive sandboxes/dev. (5) Tags for EKS compatibility: default EKS subnet role tags and cluster discovery tags are supported. By default we tag public subnets with `kubernetes.io/role/elb=1` and private subnets with `kubernetes.io/role/internal-elb=1`. We also support `kubernetes.io/cluster/<cluster_name>=shared` when `eks_cluster_name` is provided (alpha assumes cluster created elsewhere; this module only prepares network). (6) Example environment: `examples/private-eks-vpc` shows minimal inputs, expected outputs, and common overrides for enterprise CIDR requirements. Public interface (high level): Required inputs: `name`, `vpc_cidr`, `azs` (list). Common inputs: `public_subnet_cidrs`, `private_subnet_cidrs` (optional, otherwise calculated), `single_nat_gateway` (bool), `one_nat_gateway_per_az` (bool), `eks_cluster_name` (optional), `tags` (map). Outputs: `vpc_id`, `public_subnet_ids`, `private_subnet_ids`, `public_route_table_ids`, `private_route_table_ids`, `nat_gateway_ids`, `igw_id`, `azs`. Design notes / constraints (important for Redwood Private + EKS): - This module does NOT create VPC Endpoints yet. For truly “no public egress” environments, you will need endpoints from the follow-up endpoints module (tracked separately). For now, NAT provides outbound access for pulling images, talking to AWS APIs, etc. - EKS private endpoint: EKS API endpoint access mode is not set here; however, for Private deployments we assume customers will configure private endpoint access and ensure VPC DNS/resolver behavior is stable. We explicitly enable VPC DNS support/hostnames to reduce the most common private endpoint failure mode. - Ingress/egress policy: This module deliberately does not create security groups. SG patterns are split into a separate module/PR so we can iterate on least-privilege without blocking VPC composition. - AZ assumptions: the module behaves best with >=2 AZs. If you pass 1 AZ, NAT-per-AZ and CIDR calculations still work, but we consider it out of scope for “production-like” alpha deployments (documented in README). - IPv6: not included in alpha. - Isolated/data subnets: not included yet; can be added later as an extension (DB/cache patterns) without breaking the current contract. Illustrative snippet (from README): `module "vpc" { source = "../../modules/vpc" name = "acme-redwood" vpc_cidr = "10.20.0.0/16" azs = ["us-east-1a", "us-east-1b", "us-east-1c"] one_nat_gateway_per_az = true eks_cluster_name = "acme-redwood-eks" tags = { "owner" = "platform" "environment" = "poc" } }` Implementation details: - Subnet CIDR computation uses deterministic splitting by AZ index when explicit CIDRs are not provided, and validates that the number of computed CIDRs matches the AZ count. - NAT logic: when `one_nat_gateway_per_az=true` we create one EIP + NAT GW per public subnet/AZ and route each private route table to the local NAT. When `single_nat_gateway=true` we create one NAT in the first public subnet and route all private subnets to it (documented as reduced fault tolerance). Inputs are validated to prevent conflicting flags (e.g., both single NAT and per-AZ). - Tagging: all resources get `Name` plus common tags; subnets optionally receive EKS discovery tags. CI: - GitHub Actions runs `terraform fmt -check` and `terraform validate` for module + example. CI checks: `terraform-validate (ubuntu-latest) ... PASS`, `fmt ... PASS`. Review conversation highlights: - Irene Choi (Infra): requested we default to per-AZ NAT and document the cost vs reliability trade-off; also asked for explicit outputs for route table IDs to support downstream modules. Addressed in commits 4 and 5; added outputs + README section “NAT strategy”. - Nina Petrova (Private Deployments): asked to call out EKS private control plane constraints and ensure VPC DNS settings are enabled by default. Added `docs/architecture/vpc-module-design-notes.md` and README “EKS constraints” section; confirmed DNS flags in main. - Marcus Lin (Security Eng): flagged that NAT-by-default implies outbound egress and asked that we be explicit that endpoints module will be the “secure-by-default no-public-egress” path. Added README warning and a TODO list that points to endpoints module follow-up. - Hanae Suzuki (Security templates): requested we avoid creating any overly permissive SGs in the VPC module. Confirmed scope: no SGs in this PR; SG patterns are separate. - Simran Kaur (Ref arch review): asked for a diagram in docs and a clearer mapping between outputs and the installer needs. Added a short “Integration points” section listing typical consumers (installer, endpoints module, logging module). Checklist: [x] Module README includes required inputs/outputs and constraints [x] Example `private-eks-vpc` runs `terraform validate` [x] CI green [x] Notes added for extension points (endpoints, logging, connectivity hooks) Merge: Squash merged into `main` on 2025-06-09. Follow-ups: - Add endpoints module (ECR/S3/STS/CloudWatch Logs/etc.) and update example to support no-internet-egress deployments. - Add security group patterns module and align with installer preflight expectations.
